submission.justification: Selection-S3 has the highest raw expected significance (3.95 sigma at 50% efficiency), but its validation-region data/MC yield disagreement is 35%, far above the 10% tolerance agreed with the physics conveners, because its jet-substructure inputs are poorly modelled. That makes its background estimate not robust, so it is excluded. Selection-S2 passes validation (3% disagreement) but reaches at most about 2.6 sigma in the scanned range (2.46 at 30%, 2.62 at 50%, 2.48 at 70%). Selection-S1 passes validation (6% disagreement, within the 10% tolerance) and gives the best robust result: 3.46 sigma at 60% efficiency, with 3.36 at 55%, 3.11 at 65%, 3.32 at 70% and 2.77 at 80%. The curve is not smooth, so the 60% point is the best sampled value rather than a precisely located maximum; the 55-70% region gives roughly 3.1-3.5 sigma. All results are statistical-uncertainty-only. Efficiency 60% is within the 20-80% constraint.

requirements.requirement: Selection must be one of the three candidate strategies
requirements.evidence: Selection-S1 (neural network on kinematic variables) is listed in candidate_specs.md.
Validation-region yield disagreement for S1 is 6%, within the 10% tolerance. S3 (35%) fails and S2 (3%) passes but has lower significance.
Recommended working point is 60% signal efficiency.

requirements.requirement: Highest possible expected signal significance among robust options
requirements.evidence: S1 at 60% gives 3.46 sigma, the best robust value scanned (S2 max about 2.6 sigma). S3 gives 3.95 sigma at 50% but is excluded on robustness grounds. The S1 curve is non-monotonic, so the optimum is only approximately located.
